title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Marisol Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and processes that govern access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and the set of canonical internal templates. It is intended as the single source of truth for employees, managers, and approvers.

Scope:
Applies to all employees, contractors, and vendors interacting with Redwood systems, infrastructure, or data. Where applicable, sections call out additional controls for Dedicated and Private deployments.

Owners and Contact:
- Document owner: people-ops (Marisol Chen)
- Security liaison: Security (Daniel Park)
- Procurement lead: Finance (Priya Raman)
- Questions or exceptions: policies@redwood-inference.com

1) Access and Permissions

Policy summary:
- Principle: least privilege by default; role-based access; just-in-time elevation where feasible.
- All access must be requested through the Access Request portal and approved by the resource owner and the requester’s manager.

Access request workflow (numbered):
1. Employee initiates request in Access Request portal (Jira/ServiceNow ticket created).
2. Manager reviews and confirms business justification.
3. Resource owner (service/owner team) approves or denies.
4. Automation provisions access via IAM or identity provider (IdP) connectors.
5. Access is time-bound; expiration set by role classification.

Approval matrix (table-like text):
- Low-risk (read-only documentation, wiki): manager approval; default duration: 365 days.
- Medium-risk (non-prod infra, analytics): manager + resource owner; default duration: 90 days.
- High-risk (prod infra, secrets, PII): manager + resource owner + security review; default duration: 30 days; MFA and conditional access required.

Onboarding and offboarding:
- New hire access checklist is maintained by people-ops and synced to IdP.
- Offboarding must revoke all direct credentials and terminate active sessions within 4 hours of offboarding ticket completion.

Privileged access controls:
- Use ephemeral access tokens (Just-in-Time) for admin activities where possible.
- All privileged sessions must be recorded/audited (session logs stored in audit-logging service).

Periodic access reviews:
- Owner teams perform quarterly reviews for high- and medium-risk resources, annually for low-risk.

2) Change Management

Purpose:
Ensure changes to production systems are planned, risk-assessed, and communicated to reduce incidents and downtime.

Change categories and authorization:
- Standard change: low-risk, pre-approved (routine maintenance). Approved by owner team.
- Normal change: requires risk assessment, RCA (if related), and CAB approval for production-impacting changes.
- Emergency change: implemented to mitigate active incidents; must be logged and undergo post-change review within 72 hours.

Process steps (numbered):
1. Submit change request with description, affected services, rollback plan, test plan, and owner.
2. Risk classification and scheduling (owner team).
3. CAB review for Normal changes (weekly CAB; include SRE, Security, Product if customer-facing).
4. Implementation and monitoring with runbook.
5. Post-deployment verification and update runbooks.

SLOs and guardrails:
- No normal change should be scheduled during company blackout windows (major release freeze windows published quarterly).
- All production changes must include a rollback plan and automated health checks.

3) Data Management

Data classification:
- Public: information safe for external distribution.
- Internal: company operational data not PII or regulated.
- Confidential: includes customer data, internal roadmaps, and financials.
- Restricted: regulated data (PII, PHI, or customer-designated restricted datasets).

Handling requirements (bullets):
- Encrypt data at rest and in transit for Confidential and Restricted tiers (TLS + KMS-managed encryption).
- Access to Restricted data requires explicit business justification and security approval.
- Masking and minimization: only store the minimal fields required; use tokenization or hashing where practical.

Retention and deletion (table-like rules):
- Logs: retention 90 days for standard logs; 365 days for security logs (configurable per product).
- Backups: daily backups retained 30 days, monthly snapshots retained 12 months unless customer contract specifies otherwise.
- Customer data retention follows contract SLA and privacy agreements; deletion requests must be executed within contractually defined windows.

Data breach response:
- Follow the Security Incident Response runbook; notify Legal and Customer Success for customer-impacting events within 24 hours of detection.

4) Procurement and Expenses

Procurement policy summary:
- All purchases must follow the procurement workflow and be tagged with a cost center. Purchase orders (POs) are required for commitments > $5,000.
- Card purchases under $500 are allowed with manager approval; recurring SaaS subscriptions must be reviewed by Finance.

Procurement workflow (numbered):
1. Requestor submits procurement request with business justification and estimated cost.
2. Manager and cost center approver review.
3. Procurement team performs vendor validation and issues PO for approved purchases.
4. Finance codes expense to appropriate GL account.

Expense policy highlights:
- Travel: per-diem and caps defined in Travel policy below.
- Entertainment: must include attendee list and business purpose; receipts for all expenses over $75.
- Approval thresholds: manager (< $2,000), director ($2,000–$25,000), CFO (> $25,000).

5) Vendor Management

Onboarding checklist (bulleted):
- Security questionnaire (completed and evaluated).
- Contract with data processing agreement (if vendor will process customer or company data).
- Insurance verification and liability terms.
- Vendor classification (strategic, standard, transient) based on spend and sensitivity.

SLA and monitoring:
- All strategic vendors must have documented SLAs and monthly performance reviews.
- Security and privacy controls periodically evaluated (annual reviews for strategic vendors, bi-annual for others).

Termination and offboarding:
- Ensure return/destruction of company data, revocation of access, and confirmation of asset return.

6) Travel Policy (summary)

Booking and approvals:
- Employees should book travel via the approved travel portal or travel desk. International travel requires advance notice and manager approval.
- Domestic flights: standard economy; upgrades permissible with director approval.

Per-diem and allowable costs:
- Meals: per-diem $75/day in US; adjust regionally with regional multipliers.
- Hotel: standard business class; reasonable mid-tier hotels recommended.
- Ground transport: rideshare or rental car when public transit is not practical.

Expense reporting:
- Submit receipts in the expense system within 15 days of trip completion.
- Card vs personal: company card preferred for travel-related purchases.

Health and safety:
- For travel to high-risk geographies consult Security and complete travel register entry.

7) Internal Templates and Forms

Canonical templates (list):
- Access Request template (Access Request portal link)
- Change Request template (change-management ticket template)
- Vendor Onboarding checklist (procurement portal)
- Travel authorization form
- Expense report template
- Data classification decision log template

How to use templates:
- Templates live in the company templates space and are versioned. Always copy the canonical template; do not edit the master.

Exceptions and waivers
- Any deviations from these policies require a documented exception request submitted to the owner team with executive sponsor and security review for non-trivial risks. Exceptions are timeboxed and reviewed quarterly.

Audit and compliance
- Policy compliance is enforced via quarterly audits by Internal Audit and Security. Findings will be remediated according to severity and tracked to closure.

Appendices (short references)
- Access and Permissions: detailed technical playbook at /confluence/eng-infra/cloud-accounts-and-networking/access-playbook
- Change Management: CAB charter and schedule at /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/CAB
- Data Management: classification decision tree and retention matrix at /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention
- Procurement: procurement portal and vendor master list at /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process

Revision history:

- 2028-09-12: Updated procurement thresholds and PO requirements (Finance).
- 2029-11-20: Clarified retention rules for backups and security log retention (People-ops + Security).

End of document.
